newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Lawyers move to stop Nigerian treason trial.
newsitem.headline: Lawyers move to stop Nigerian treason trial.

text.p: More than 20 defence lawyers for Nigerian dissidents charged with treason over recent bomb blasts in the country asked a court on Friday to strike out the case.
The 12 dissidents, including exiled Nobel laureate Wole Soyinka, were charged in March and face the death penalty if convicted.
Lagos human rights activist and lawyer Gani Fawehinmi, leading other opposition lawyers, told the magistrate that her court was incompetent to hear such a serious charge.
"Nothing fruitful can come out of incompetence because the accused have been wrongly charged in the wrong court," he said.

Along with Soyinka, others charged in absentia are some exiled leaders of the opposition group NADECO, including former army chief Lieutenant-General Alani Akinrinade and information minister Anthony Enahoro.
Eight of the dissidents are in the country but were not brought to court on Friday.
The magistrate adjourned to Tuesday next week to rule on the plea that the case should be struck out, a plea fiercely opposed by government lawyer Nuhu Ribadu.
The accused face a two count charge of "conspiracy to levy war against the federal military government of Nigeria" and "causing explosions in various parts of Nigeria."
The accused include Frederick Fasehun, president of the Campaign for Democracy pressure group and former finance minister Olu Falae.
Both men have been detained since December after a spate of bomb explosions hit army buses, killing at least three soldiers and wounding several dozens.
The most recent bomb blast occurred in Lagos on Wednesday wounding five soldiers, although not seriously.

The U.S. embassy in Lagos said on Friday that one of its Nigerian employees, who happened to be driving on his usual route along the Herbert Macauley way to work at the time of the explosion, was being questioned by police over Wednesday's bomb.
"The U.S. embassy wishes to reiterate the U.S. government's complete rejection of terrorism for any position," it said in a statement.
